summary: Fluvoxamine is an SSRI indicated for obsessive-compulsive disorder. It carries a boxed warning for increased suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents, and young adults. It is a potent inhibitor of several CYP450 enzymes (notably CYP1A2 and CYP2C19), making it prone to drug interactions, and it is contraindicated with several agents including thioridazine, tizanidine, pimozide, alosetron, and ramelteon.

dosage.d: Start 100 mg at bedtime; increase by 50 mg weekly as tolerated
dosage.n: Not to exceed 300 mg/day; do not crush or chew capsules

dosage.d: Start 50 mg at bedtime; increase by 50 mg every 4-7 days
dosage.t: Once daily at bedtime; divide doses above 100 mg into two (give larger dose at bedtime)

dosage.d: Start 25 mg at bedtime; increase by 25 mg every 4-7 days
dosage.t: Divide doses above 50 mg, giving larger dose at bedtime
dosage.n: Max 200 mg/day (8-11 yr) or 300 mg/day (adolescents); titrate slowly in girls

dosage.d: Lower starting dose with slower titration
dosage.n: Decreased clearance may require dose modification

admin: Take at bedtime; with or without food
Swallow extended-release capsules whole - do not crush or chew
Titrate gradually to the lowest effective dose
Taper gradually when discontinuing to reduce withdrawal symptoms
moa: Fluvoxamine is a potent and selective inhibitor of the neuronal serotonin (5-HT) reuptake transporter, increasing serotonergic neurotransmission. It has no significant affinity for histaminergic, adrenergic, muscarinic, or dopaminergic receptors, which limits sedative, anticholinergic, and cardiovascular effects relative to tricyclics.

absolute: Coadministration with thioridazine, tizanidine, pimozide, alosetron, or ramelteon
MAO inhibitors for psychiatric disorders, or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI; do not start an MAOI within 14 days of stopping fluvoxamine
Concurrent linezolid or intravenous methylene blue
monitor: Suicidality (especially <25 years and early in therapy)

preg: Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Neonates exposed to SSRIs late in the third trimester have developed complications requiring respiratory support and tube feeding; there may be a small increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage and of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn.
lact: Fluvoxamine is secreted in human breast milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or the drug, weighing the importance of the drug to the mother.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is provided for renal impairment, but titrate cautiously as for any SSRI and monitor tolerability.
hepatic: Decreased clearance in hepatic impairment may require a lower starting dose and slower titration; monitor closely.

major: MAO inhibitors, linezolid, IV methylene blue (serotonin syndrome - contraindicated)
Thioridazine, pimozide, tizanidine, alosetron, ramelteon (contraindicated - CYP inhibition raises levels)
Other serotonergic drugs (triptans, tramadol, lithium, St. John's wort)
Theophylline, clozapine, olanzapine, caffeine (CYP1A2 inhibition raises levels)
moderate: Warfarin and other CYP2C9 substrates (raised levels / bleeding)
minor: Smoking (induces CYP1A2 and lowers fluvoxamine exposure)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor INR with warfarin and serum sodium in at-risk patients

monitoring: Suicidality and mood, especially early and after dose changes
Serum sodium in elderly / at-risk patients
INR in patients on warfarin and signs of bleeding
counsel: Benefit in OCD may take several weeks to develop
Take the extended-release capsule whole at bedtime; do not crush or chew
Do not stop abruptly - taper to avoid withdrawal symptoms
Avoid alcohol and limit caffeine (levels may rise)
Report worsening mood, agitation, or thoughts of self-harm immediately
Tell your prescriber about all medicines - fluvoxamine has many interactions
pk: Anti-obsessional benefit develops over several weeks
IR usually given once daily/divided; ER once daily
Store at 25 C (77 F); protect from high humidity; avoid above 30 C
pearls: Boxed warning: increased suicidality in children, adolescents, and young adults - monitor closely
Potent inhibitor of CYP1A2 and CYP2C19 (also 2C9/3A4) - a major source of drug interactions
Contraindicated with thioridazine, tizanidine, pimozide, alosetron, and ramelteon
Raises clozapine, olanzapine, theophylline, and caffeine levels via CYP1A2 inhibition
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose may cause drowsiness, vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, tachycardia or bradycardia, hypotension, ECG changes, convulsions, serotonin syndrome, coma, and (rarely, especially in mixed ingestions) death. Management is supportive with airway protection and cardiac monitoring; activated charcoal may help if given early. There is no specific antidote; forced diuresis and dialysis are unlikely to be beneficial given high protein binding and volume of distribution.
